shortcut_name: degenerate experiments reduce to three simple totals
evidence: deepseek: "if job_bottleneck is not None" followed by "elif sum_p1 > T"; gpt-oss: "look for a job that exceeds T alone" and then "total_p1 = sum(p1)"; qwen: "Experiment 1: Check if any job itself takes more than T" and "LOAD 1 - Serial capacitor charges"; glm: "only precedence per job" and "total_p1 = sum(p1)"
affordance_in_statement: Experiment Type 1 ignores both grid capacities; Experiment Type 2 sets all System Initialization durations to 0 and removes the initialization grid capacity; Experiment Type 3 sets all Capacitor Charge durations to 0 and removes the capacitor grid capacity.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: these clauses define experiments whose optimal makespans are intrinsically p1[i]+p2[i], sum(p1), and sum(p2). To make the task non-degenerate, the experiments would need to retain nonzero work and both interacting resources, which changes the computational task rather than merely rewording it.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses per-job p1+p2, then total p1, and implicitly total p2 for the three experiments.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The experiments remove capacities or set one burst duration to zero.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Scans for any p1+p2>T, then checks the aggregate p1 load.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Experiment 1 is independent per subsystem, while Experiment 2 is just serial capacitor work.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly treats Experiment 1 as an individual-job check and Experiment 2 as a serial sum.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Zero-duration initialization and unlimited initialization capacity make only the capacitor total relevant.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Directly implements the three closed-form checks rather than scheduling.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement says Experiment 1 has only precedence and Experiment 2 has only serial capacitor work.

common_affordance: The three hypothetical schedules are deliberately degenerate: precedence makes a single job take p1+p2, and eliminating one resource plus zeroing the other burst type makes the remaining makespan a simple sum.
recommended_edit: Replace the zero-duration and capacity-removal experiment definitions with experiments that preserve nonzero durations and interaction between both grids, so each experiment requires an actual two-machine schedule rather than p1+p2, sum(p1), or sum(p2).
